commands.result: Dry run only. Security mode 1 (prod/encrypted), challenge enabled, max 2 participants, app version 26, LDN version 4, protocol 1, application data 4 bytes, frame format aes-ctr, frame length 1364 bytes, round-trip decode OK (11 fields match). SSID and frame hex were not printed.
Host started, advertised, and stopped cleanly. The log ended with 'Host stopped. Join events observed: 0.'
Captured 660 beacons, 373 vendor action frames, and 10 data frames from the host adapter. No frames from the console.
Captured 1222 beacons, 655 vendor action frames, and 19 data frames from the host adapter. No frames from the console.

Three attempts returned FOUND with rssi -90 and channel 6; a later attempt returned FOUND with rssi -94 and channel 13. Every result had a nil BSSID. A control scan for a random non-existent 16-byte SSID also returned FOUND (rssi -81, channel 1, nil BSSID).

frame_validation.method: Decoded the first captured host advertisement with the owner's local keys and KeyDerivation(protocol=1).
frame_validation.result: The advertisement decrypted and its SHA-256 validated.
frame_validation.note: The host frame matches the Phase 1 room's decrypted fields. The participant name length differs because the host uses the local name TX10LED.

adapter_tx.note: The capture on the host's own phy proves that the frames reached the monitor interfaces, but it does not prove RF transmission. The rtw88_8822bu driver may loop back injected frames, and it logged one new 'failed to get tx report from firmware' message. An independent receiver is still required.

directed_scan.method: macOS CoreWLAN scanForNetworks(withSSID:) for the 16-byte room SSID
directed_scan.control: A scan for a random non-existent 16-byte SSID also returned FOUND (rssi=-81, channel=1, bssid=<nil>).
directed_scan.validity: INVALID as a transmission check. The API returns a false positive for a non-existent 16-byte SSID with a nil BSSID and an inconsistent channel, so a FOUND result cannot be attributed to the host.
directed_scan.conclusion: Do not use the directed CoreWLAN scan as a TX check. Use a wildcard scan for the host BSSID or a second receiver instead.

wildcard_bssid_check.method: macOS CoreWLAN scanForNetworks(withSSID: nil) and compare CWNetwork.bssid to the host adapter BSSID
wildcard_bssid_check.result: The host BSSID was not present in 6 scan results with the host stopped.
wildcard_bssid_check.validity: This is the independent check to run during the next approved host run. It does not rely on the broken directed-SSID matching.

authorization: The owner approved one short prod-mode host run with the existing local keys, a directed SSID scan, and a capture. This record covers that run. Another active run requires new explicit approval.
interpretation: The prod-mode host built and transmitted 373 AES-CTR advertisements whose decrypted fields match the target's Phase 1 room, including the SSID, application data, challenge, max participants, and app version. The host logged no JOIN, the console reported no rooms after a roughly one-second search, and the capture saw no frames from the console. The same-phy capture and the invalid directed scan do not independently prove that the frames were on air; the rtw88_8822bu driver may loop back injected frames, and it logged one new TX-report failure. The result is therefore inconclusive about RF transmission and does not show that the console rejected the prod-mode room.
limitations: The same-phy capture is not an independent receiver; it may see injected frames that never reached the air.
The macOS directed-SSID scan is invalid because it returns false positives for non-existent 16-byte SSIDs.
The console screen was observed by the owner, not captured automatically.
The console's roughly one-second search duration is an owner report, not a measurement.
Only one game and one prod-mode room were tested.
Firmware was not re-queried during this run.
The SSID, interface name, and MAC addresses are redacted.
